data.name: Nazaire
data.gender_notes: Nazaire is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Nazareth means ‘flower of the valley’. Nazaire is a name given to Jesus by the angel Gabriel when announcing his birth to the Virgin Mary in the New Testament. This name is symbolic of the Savior’s humble beginnings and his destiny to grow and flourish. The name Nazaire carries the meaning “Named by an angel” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nazaire usually hope their child will grow to embody named by an angel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of humility and the growth of one's spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Nazaire belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Named by an angel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nazaire total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: נזיר
in_hebrew.meaning: השם נזיר מתייחס לנזיר או לקדוש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם נזיר נגזר מהמילה העברית 'נזר', שפירושה 'נזיר' או 'קדוש'. הוא מתייחס לאדם שנדר להיות נזיר או קדוש, והוא קשור לקונספט של הקדשה והתמסרות לאלוהים. השם נזיר מופיע בתנ"ך ככינוי לאדם שנדר להיות נזיר, כמו למשל בנזירותו של שמשון. השם נזיר הוא גם קשור לקדושים ולנזירים הנוצרים, שראו בו דוגמה לחיים של הקדשה וצניעות.

in_greek.name: Ναζαίρη
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Ναζαίρη σημαίνει αγιασμένος ή Consecrated
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ναζαίρη προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'נזר' (Nazir), που σημαίνει 'αγιασμένος' ή 'consecrated'. Στη Βίβλο, ο όρος 'Ναζαίρη' αναφέρεται σε ένα άτομο που έχει αφιερώσει τον εαυτό του στον Θεό, ζώντας μια ζωή αφιερωμένη και αγνή. Ο όρος αυτός συνδέεται με την έννοια της πνευματικής αφιέρωσης και της θρησκευτικής ευλάβειας. Στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία, ο όρος 'Ναζαίρη' χρησιμοποιήθηκε για να περιγράψει εκείνους που είχαν αφιερώσει τις ζωές τους στον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Nazaire
in_latin.meaning: Nazaire means consecrated or holy one
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Nazaire is derived from the Hebrew word 'נזר' (Nazir), meaning 'consecrated' or 'holy one'. In the early Christian Church, the term 'Nazaire' referred to an individual who had dedicated their life to God, living a life of devotion and piety. The name Nazaire is associated with the concept of spiritual dedication and religious devotion. Throughout Christian tradition, the name Nazaire has been borne by several saints and martyrs, symbolizing their commitment to their faith.

in_english.name: Nazaire
in_english.meaning: Nazaire means consecrated or holy one in Christian tradition
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nazaire originates from the Hebrew word 'נזר' (Nazir), meaning 'consecrated' or 'holy one'. It is associated with the biblical concept of a Nazirite, an individual who has taken a vow of dedication to God, often involving a life of asceticism and piety. In Christian tradition, the name Nazaire has been borne by several saints and martyrs, symbolizing their commitment to their faith. The name Nazaire conveys a sense of spiritual dedication, devotion, and holiness, reflecting the values of Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nazareth and Nazaire have root in the biblical city and the Virgin Mary's son who lived there. This name, while not common in everyday usage, has reverberated throughout history as a reminder of Christ's humble origins and the importance of faith in overcoming adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nazareth and Nazaire hold significant spiritual meaning for Christians, representing the belief that even in the most humble and unassuming of beginnings, an individual can grow into something great, with God's grace and guidance. It is a reminder of the importance of having faith and trusting in God, regardless of the circumstances.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nazareth was the hometown of Jesus, signifying His humble roots and connection to humanity. The name "Nazaire" symbolizes the commitment to follow in Jesus' footsteps, embracing both His divine and human natures. It is a reminder to live a simple, grounded life rooted in faith and service to others.

biblical_reference.note: The term 'Nazirite' refers to an individual who has taken a vow of dedication to God.

historical_references.reference: Legend holds that Joseph, Mary's husband, was advised in a dream to take the baby Jesus to Egypt to escape the massacre of the innocents ordered by King Herod. They settled in the city of Nazareth.

The name Nazareth is believed to have derived from the Hebrew word 'Nazir' meaning 'consecrated', 'dedicated' or 'pure'. This would have been a fitting name for Jesus, as he was believed to be the son of God and free from sin.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Nazarene' or 'Nazaire' is derived from the Biblical town of Nazareth where Jesus is said to have spent his childhood. In modern context, it has expanded beyond its Christian roots and is used in various non-religious contexts. In Christian spirituality, it is used to refer to followers of certain denominations, such as the Nazarene Church or the Church of the Nazarene. In the realm of New Age philosophy, it is adopted as a personal name or identifier, symbolizing self-transcendence, spiritual awakening or connection to nature. In mythology, it can be used as a symbol of spiritual transformation, resistance or protection. Nazarene/Nazaire is often explored in spiritual retreats, metaphysical bookstores, and online forums where individuals seek to deepen their understanding of personal growth, spirituality, and the meaning of life.
